title: Security docs publication plan (Marketplace refresh)
content:
Purpose
This doc defines what Redwood Inference security/compliance content is published publicly on the docs site vs shared as gated content vs provided on-request (NDA / controlled distribution). It also defines the review workflow, ownership, and versioning so the AWS + GCP marketplace security review can proceed without conflicting statements across Confluence, docs.redwoodinference.com, and sales/shared attachments.

Scope
- Marketplace-facing security documentation bundle (AWS + GCP)
- Customer security questionnaire acceleration (standard answers + evidence pointers)
- Ongoing maintenance after marketplace launch (quarterly reviews + change log)

Non-goals
- Writing new controls/evidence from scratch (tracked separately in PM-1847 and GRC workstream)
- Publishing confidential internal evidence (audit reports, pen test full reports, vendor contracts)

Primary audiences
1) Marketplace reviewers (AWS/GCP partner security review teams)
2) Security teams at enterprise buyers (questionnaires, architecture review)
3) Procurement + legal stakeholders (data handling, sub-processors, retention/residency)
4) Technical evaluators (how logging, encryption, key management, and access controls work)

Guiding principles (agreed in Docs + Security thread 1769395510)
- Accurate, current, and consistent: security claims must match product behavior and contractual commitments.
- Tiered disclosure: publish enough to pass marketplace review and accelerate buyer diligence without oversharing sensitive evidence.
- “Explain the system” > “promise the world”: document capabilities, defaults, and configuration options; avoid absolute statements unless contractually true.
- Shared responsibility is explicit: what Redwood operates vs what customer configures in Dedicated/Private.
- Versioned + attributable: every published security page has an “Effective date” and change log.

Distribution channels
A) Public docs site (docs.redwoodinference.com)
- Goal: make marketplace buyers self-serve answers for common questions.
- Must be reviewed/approved for wording sensitivity.
- Must avoid disclosing sensitive internal details (exact tooling, detection thresholds, internal network topology, non-public sub-processor specifics beyond what’s already published).

B) Gated security portal (access controlled; “request access”)
- Goal: share higher-fidelity artifacts (e.g., SOC 2 report under NDA, pen test executive summary, detailed subprocessor list, DPA templates).
- Access is logged and time-bounded.
- Only shared after buyer identity + email domain verification; NDA where required.

C) On-request (manual, case-by-case)
- Goal: provide any additional evidence required by regulated prospects (fintech/health/insurance) that does not fit portal distribution.
- Requires Security/GRC approval and sometimes Legal approval.

Publication matrix (what goes where)

1) Security overview (marketplace-friendly)
- Content: high-level program summary, control areas, compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II), secure SDLC summary, incident response overview.
- Location: Public docs site
- Owner: Naomi Feldman (Security/compliance product) + Elliot Price (Docs)
- Review required: Dr. Aisha Rahman (exec sponsor), Sofia Mendes (commercial counsel) for claims
- Notes: Avoid stating “ISO 27001 certified” unless formally certified; if in progress, state “aligned with” + clarify status.

2) Shared responsibility model (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Content: responsibility split for identity access, network controls, logging, key management, backups, data retention controls.
- Location: Public docs site
- Owner: Marcus Lin (Security Eng) + Kira Thompson (Dedicated/Private writer)
- Notes: Must match product reality, especially for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem): what Redwood provides vs customer-managed.

3) Data handling + retention + residency
- Content: what data is processed (prompts/outputs/metadata), default retention, customer-configurable retention, residency commitments by deployment type, backup and deletion behavior.
- Location: Public docs site (capabilities + defaults); deeper implementation notes in Gated portal
- Owner: Olga Petrov (GRC) + Wei Chen (writer)
- Notes: This page is frequently cited in procurement; include “Last reviewed” date.

4) Encryption + key management (KMS/HSM integrations)
- Content: encryption in transit, encryption at rest, key management options per deployment mode, customer-managed keys where supported.
- Location: Public docs site
- Owner: Marcus Lin
- Review: Security claims review required (avoid naming internal services/vendors unless already public)

5) Audit logs
- Content: what events are logged (auth, org/admin, API key creation, model config/rollout changes), export options, retention, SIEM integration notes.
- Location: Public docs site
- Owner: Marcus Lin + Alex Martinez
- Notes: Must align with actual audit log event coverage; do not claim events not yet implemented.

6) Subprocessors
- Content: list of subprocessors used for Hosted and for control plane; purpose; region relevance.
- Location: Gated portal (preferred) OR public if already published as part of standard trust page. 
- Owner: Olga Petrov
- Legal review: required
- Notes: Marketplace reviewers sometimes expect a link; if gated, publish a public stub page that explains how to request the current list.

7) SOC 2 Type II report
- Content: report PDF
- Location: Gated portal only
- Owner: Olga Petrov
- Process: NDA required depending on customer; portal access logs required.

8) Pen test summary
- Content: executive summary + remediation status
- Location: Gated portal (default) / on-request for stricter customers
- Owner: Marcus Lin + Olga Petrov

9) Vulnerability management and disclosure
- Content: vulnerability management overview, patch timelines (ranges, not exact), security.txt / disclosure email, CVE handling.
- Location: Public docs site
- Owner: Marcus Lin

10) Incident response and customer notification
- Content: high-level IR lifecycle, notification principles, status page link, support channels.
- Location: Public docs site
- Owner: Naomi Feldman
- Notes: avoid committing to specific hour-based timelines unless contractual in SLA.

11) Marketplace “security packet” index page
- Content: a navigable index that points to public docs pages and indicates which artifacts are available gated/on-request.
- Location: Public docs site
- Owner: Elliot Price
- Notes: This is the primary page referenced in AWS/GCP marketplace submission attachments.

Canonical source of truth + duplication rules
- Confluence is internal working source (drafts, evidence pointers, internal-only details).
- Docs site is canonical for customer-facing claims.
- If a Confluence page is customer-facing-ready, it must be either:
  (a) migrated into docs site as the canonical copy, or
  (b) explicitly labeled “INTERNAL REFERENCE — do not share externally” and a separate docs page is created.

Naming + URL strategy (needed for marketplace forms)
- Stable URLs; avoid renames in the 2-week window around submission.
- Proposed URLs (finalize in INT-771 redirects request):
  - /security/overview
  - /security/shared-responsibility
  - /security/data-handling-retention
  - /security/encryption-key-management
  - /security/audit-logs
  - /security/marketplace-security-packet
  - /security/subprocessors (public stub + request link)

Review + approval workflow

Roles
- Docs DRI: Elliot Price (ensures publishability, formatting, IA)
- Security DRI: Naomi Feldman (ensures claims match policy + commitments)
- Security Eng reviewer: Marcus Lin (ensures technical accuracy)
- GRC/evidence reviewer: Olga Petrov (ensures compliance posture + evidence pointers)
- Legal reviewer: Sofia Mendes / Michael Grant (claims, commitments, subprocessors/disclosures)
- GTM/Marketplaces reviewer: Soojin Lee + Jordan Blake (positioning; avoid competitive or risky language)

Workflow (for any page that contains security claims)
1) Draft in GitHub PR (docs repo) OR in Confluence with an explicit “to be migrated” tag.
2) Security technical review (Marcus) + compliance review (Olga) in-line.
3) Legal review trigger conditions:
   - Statements that could be construed as contractual (SLA, notification timing, certifications)
   - Subprocessor disclosures
   - Data residency commitments
4) Final approval: Naomi (Security) + Elliot (Docs)
5) Publish + record version in change log.
6) Update marketplace submission artifacts (AWS/GCP portals) if URLs or summaries changed.

SLA for review turnaround (target)
- Standard updates: 3 business days for Security review; 5 business days if Legal review required.
- Pre-submission freeze window: no non-critical wording changes within 5 business days of marketplace resubmission unless required by partner feedback.

Versioning + maintenance

Versioning scheme
- Each top-level security page includes:
  - Effective date (YYYY-MM-DD)
  - Version (vMAJOR.MINOR)
  - “Last reviewed” date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Meaning:
  - MAJOR: changes in commitments/capabilities that materially affect buyer evaluation (e.g., default retention changed, new deployment mode behavior)
  - MINOR: clarifications, formatting, non-material additions

Change log
- Maintained on /security/marketplace-security-packet with a short entry per change (date, page, summary, link to PR).

Maintenance cadence
- Quarterly review: Security + Docs (Naomi/Elliot) and GRC (Olga)
- Trigger-based review:
  - New SKU/packaging impacts retention/logging/keys
  - New regions/residency commitments
  - Product changes affecting audit logs or data storage
  - Incident learnings that require doc changes

Evidence links hygiene (Gated portal)
- Evidence links expire/rotate; owners must refresh within 10 business days of rotation.
- Portal access list reviewed monthly (remove stale access).

Marketplace submission alignment
- AWS/GCP reviewers often screenshot pages; ensure pages render without auth and have stable headings.
- Any PDF attachments referenced by marketplace forms must match the public docs content (no conflicting retention numbers, encryption statements, etc.).

Operational checklist (pre-launch / pre-submission)
- [ ] Public pages are live and indexed from /security/marketplace-security-packet
- [ ] Subprocessors stub page is live (with request workflow)
- [ ] Gated portal access workflow tested end-to-end (request → approval → access log)
- [ ] Security packet language reviewed vs marketplace listing claims (copy must be consistent)
- [ ] Links verified (no 404s) and redirects in place (INT-771)
- [ ] Sales/SE “security packet” snippet updated in enablement docs (FAQ macros + questionnaire responses)

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Do we publish the high-level subprocessor list publicly or keep it gated with a public stub? (Owner: Olga + Legal)
2) Do we include a dedicated “Model data usage” statement (prompts/outputs not used for training by default; any opt-in programs)? Needs careful wording. (Owner: Naomi + Legal)
3) For Private (on-prem), what minimal statement do we publish about customer responsibility for physical security and hypervisor-level controls? (Owner: Marcus + Colin O’Donnell)

Risks + mitigations
- Risk: Overpromising (claims that don’t match product defaults).
  Mitigation: security engineering review required for pages touching logs/retention/keys.
- Risk: Conflicting statements across Confluence, PDFs, and docs site.
  Mitigation: docs site is canonical; Confluence labeled internal; quarterly audit.
- Risk: Marketplace submission delay due to missing stable URLs.
  Mitigation: finalize URL list and redirect plan before partner review round 2.

Near-term timeline (targeted to marketplace refresh)
- Week of 2026-01-27: finalize publication matrix + URL plan; open redirect ticket (INT-771)
- Week of 2026-02-03: publish core pages + packet index (PR-3422)
- Week of 2026-02-10: validate gated portal workflows; confirm artifacts for AWS/GCP submission

Notes to self (Docs)
- Keep the marketplace security packet page short and navigable. Reviewers scan.
- Add “Need help?” contact block with support routing (marketplace@ alias if exists; otherwise Support + SE escalation path).
- Ensure we don’t use ambiguous terms like “fully compliant” without specificity.
